akifusenet,

You're asking some very good questions which I was asking myself a month or so ago!! I don't have all the solutions but hopefully what I've learned is of some help. First, about the significance of flag limits...some of them are more "localized" flag limits. For example, FL1 is an engulf of a local high, while FL2 is more of an engulf of the flag area to the left (where we see price meandering around without any new poles). To me that tells me FL2 is probably the more significant than FL1 since we're engulfing a larger zone. FL3 is another story of price engulfing a smaller flag area, but it did work nicely several times as you see.

Now onto the more difficult question which I've been searching for as well...FL2 - was it engulfed or not? I don't think so. First, I'm not entirely sure that FL2 is the actual flag limit or not. On the M1 chart where you can't zoom much farther unless you have a tick chart, it's possible that the actual FL extends closer to the "SR" area. If it doesn't and price did move below it, I still see this as an FTR which would show up on higher time frames as a FL in its own right (they are the same thing). Note how price broke above the S/R, tried to get back in, and then moved above the original breakout high, confirming an FTR. Where would I place the stop? Well, I wouldn't have been completely comfortable with that original FL2 zone for previously mentioned reasons, but if I were, I would have placed it a pip or so below the base of it given this is an M1 chart. If I were stopped out, I would have probably given the FTR a try as well since it's valid too. Others might put it beyond the S/R but that isn't something I care to do. Note how in your bottom center graphic that FL2 may have been exceeded by a pip or so but if you use the FTR area it would have stayed within bounds.

Significance of FL/FTR has nothing to do with time but with what kind of flag area was engulfed. Are we looking at a strong engulf of a huge daily flag area or are we looking at price engulfing a local flag on the M1? That's what makes the difference in my experience.

Keep in mind this is just my two cents, but I hope it helps. This is an area of interest for me as well.

Hi akifusenet,

Yes and no. I prefer to consider the whole area, from the top of the initial breakout, to the lowest point it retraced to before passing the breakout level, the "FTR". This matches what we do with Flag Limits. If you zoom in on a flag limit, you'll notice they are similar to FTRs which is why they're really the same concept, in just a different viewpoint.

Hi everyone. I'm going to start posting here as much as I can. I've spent the last few days going through every post in this thread so I'm pretty much up to speed on FL but its time for me to do some homework and hopefully contribute here. Special thanks to harry, I have picked up so many gems from you throughout this thread.

After reading all the posts here Im pretty comfortable with what a fl looks like so I'm not going to just post 10 flag limits here as there are so many others are in this thread. One area that I would like to spend some homework on though, is analyzing price on ltf, when we appear to be breaking a htf level.

So for my first example I'm posting an hourly chart, with 10 levels marked where we could/should be looking for flag limits. Some of them are obvious just from the hourly chart, some are invisible on the hourly chart. Lets see what we find out. I'm trying to imagine that I was doing this in real time on the charts (looking at ltf as we appear to be breaking hourly levels).

Hourly Chart with 10 important levels

Lower time frame inspection of those levels:

Level 1 shows a pretty nice looking 5 minute FL at the hourly level. Price never got back to it, but would have been a good zone I think:

Level 2 we can see there was indecision on the hourly bar, and on 5 minute we can see that there was actually a trade opportunity as well. given that there was a retest trade on 5 minute, which is invisible on htf i'm not sure what this means for any htf retests that might yet happen (I read that there are examples of this thinking in drswings journal, so i will get to that)

Level 3 we can see a bit of indicision on hourly chart, and a fairly nice looking 1 minute FL zone which didnt get tested.

Level 4 we can see a FL just on the hourly chart. We can see it more closely on 5 minute, but there was no trade entry.

Level 5 we can see the indicision on the hourly chart and zooming into 5 minute we can see the zone but there was no trade opp

Level 6 just looks like one massive bearish bar on hourly however on 5 minute there was possibly a trade. The problem with it is the flag go retested so quickly, you couldnt be sure in real time if the flag was just a little bigger than what you had just drawn and was only now making its actual low. So possible, but unlikely trade.

Level 7 we can see indicision on hourly and a very nice trade on ltf

Level 8 again looks like a big bearish bar on hourly. Best I could find on ltf was a messy looking FL on 1 minute

Level 9 we can see the hourly FL and possible hourly trade entry. The ltf looked like a flag that was gonna happen but didnt. Only the hourly flag made sense here.

Level 10 is the FL thats not visible on hourly, but can be seen on 5 minute. There is a ton of HTF (not seen on this chart) supply up there, so you would never be looking for longs, but worth looking at:

What is the takeaway for this assignment? Seems like hunting for ltf flags from hourly levels is a really good idea so long as you're aware of the bigger picture s/d zones

There are times when a HTF FL zone looks untested and good for a trade, but when we zoom in we can see there was also a ltf zone which was tested and would have been a good trade. What does this mean for our HTF zone - I will investigate and present results ASAP

Amit, the boundaries are not strict enough. Even in the D1 view you captured, it can be adjusted. LTF digging will tighten it up even further potentially (often necessary as many FL are not represented accurately in HTF).

Make it a point to distinguish the important FL and reason for it (seen from the left on the chart...ie another FL, SR, S/D).

A word of advice with flags, scope out as many as you can on every screen capture. Dig into LTF and tighten up the extremes. Watch for PA on return and break/engulf afterwards. You will notice PA reacts nicely to both sides of FL's.
